title: Vijay's Farewell Film Jana Nayagan Opens to Packed Theaters and Mixed Reviews
excerpt: The Tamil superstar-turned-Chief Minister's final cinematic outing draws massive first-day crowds, but critics remain split on its blend of fan service and political messaging.
body:
One Last Dance for Thalapathy

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay's final film, Jana Nayagan, hit theaters worldwide on Wednesday to the kind of reception reserved for cultural events rather than mere movie premieres. Fans lined up before dawn at cinemas across Tamil Nadu, performing milk abhishekam on cutouts and bursting firecrackers as the first shows began. By 11:45 AM IST, the political action thriller had already crossed ₹5 crore net from 4,175 tracked shows, according to Sacnilk, with over 107,000 tickets sold on BookMyShow in the first five hours.

https://x.com/filmfare/status/2080225583741759968 https://youtube.com/watch?v=y380B_Ci9zQ

Directed by H. Vinoth and produced by Venkat K. Narayana's KVN Productions on a reported ₹300 crore budget, Jana Nayagan carries the weight of being Vijay's swansong after more than three decades and over 65 films in Tamil cinema.

Plot and Cast

Vijay plays Thalapathy Vetri Kondan, a former police officer who adopts a young girl named Viji after she loses her father. As he trains her to overcome her fears and pursue a military career, a chance discovery of a suspicious toy leads him into a criminal network operating through a toy import front. Bobby Deol plays the primary antagonist, while the ensemble includes Pooja Hegde as a journalist and love interest, Mamitha Baiju as the adopted daughter, Prakash Raj, Priyamani, Gautham Vasudev Menon, and veteran actress Revathi.

The screenplay, co-written by H. Vinoth and Anil Ravipudi, is partly adapted from the 2023 Telugu film Bhagavanth Kesari, starring Nandamuri Balakrishna.

Critics Split Down the Middle

Reviews have landed squarely in the middle. Pinkvilla gave the film 3 out of 5 stars, calling it "a grand and fitting farewell" but noting that "general audiences may find parts of it less engaging." India Forums was slightly more generous at 3.5 stars, writing that the film "serves as an emotional farewell to Vijay, blending mass entertainment with political undertones."

"Being associated with Jana Nayagan is not something I look at as an achievement or a milestone; it is a responsibility. Vijay sir is not just a star; he is a phenomenon whose journey has shaped generations of audiences."

— Venkat K. Narayana, Producer, KVN Productions

Anirudh Ravichander's background score has drawn near-universal praise, with Pinkvilla's review noting that "few composers could have complemented this film as effectively." The father-daughter dynamic between Vijay and Mamitha Baiju has also resonated, giving the film its emotional core. On the flip side, critics have flagged preachy dialogue, Pooja Hegde's underwritten role, and uneven visual effects.

A Turbulent Path to the Screen

Jana Nayagan's journey to theaters was anything but smooth. Originally slated for Pongal 2026, the film faced months of certification delays. The Central Board of Film Certification eventually granted an A certificate, but with 12 significant cuts — many targeting the film's political undertones, including the muting of the acronym "TVK," which mirrors Vijay's real-life political party, Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam. The film was also leaked online before release, leading to arrests. A last-minute legal challenge at the Madras High Court briefly stayed the CBFC clearance before being resolved.

Audiences in the UK have access to an uncut version of the film.

Box Office Outlook

Early numbers suggest a massive opening. The film secured ₹21.26 crore in day-one advance bookings including block seats and sold over 731,000 tickets on BookMyShow before release — placing it fifth among recent Indian pre-sellers, behind Coolie, Leo, The GOAT, and Jailer. Industry trackers project a domestic opening in the ₹50-60 crore range, according to Filmfare.

Overseas, the film opened to approximately $2 million in early tracking across North America and other markets, with the Tamil version leading at 55% occupancy nationally.

A Farewell Beyond Cinema

For the Indian diaspora, particularly South Indians abroad, Jana Nayagan is more than a movie — it is the final opportunity to watch a generational icon on the big screen. Vijay's party TVK swept to power with 108 seats in the Tamil Nadu assembly elections, and his transition from reel to real politics has been a dominant narrative in South Indian pop culture. As producer Narayana put it at Vijay's swearing-in ceremony, according to The Hindu Business Line: "He has turned out to be Jana Nayagan — a man of the people — for the people of Tamil Nadu."
